FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.86  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` can be called after the FSM is already terminal, and it mutates subsystem state before crashing on transition.** There is no guard at entry like `if self.fsm.is_terminal: raise ...`. As written, a caller can invoke `process_round()` after termination; the method will still emit events, run failure detection, append performance history, update convergence and diminishing-returns state, and only then fail when `self.fsm.transition(event)` raises `RuntimeError`. That leaves the manager in a partially mutated post-terminal state with no `RoundResult` appended, corrupting auditability and making retries non-idempotent. PROPOSED_FIX: reject `process_round()` immediately when `fsm.is_terminal`, before any side effects; alternatively make post-terminal processing explicitly supported and append an immutable terminal audit record.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The manager accepts responses for models that are not part of the configured pool and lets them create persistent state.** `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` uses `setdefault` on `_perf_history`, and `get_recovery()` / `_record_failure()` also `setdefault` histories, so an unknown `model_id` in `responses` silently creates new entries even though `self.models` does not contain that model. `process_round()` also records role-assignment failures for arbitrary IDs. This is distinct from merely trusting caller-supplied IDs in findings: it allows non-member models to poison performance/failure state and appear in emitted events. PROPOSED_FIX: validate every response key and `response.model_id` against the manager’s model set before any processing; reject or quarantine unknown models.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.79  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` trusts the `responses` dict keys instead of the `ModelResponse.model_id` payload, allowing state to be written under the wrong model.** The loop iterates `for model_id, response in responses.items():` but passes `response` to `detect_failure()` and separately records failure history under the dict key `model_id`. If the key and payload disagree, failure detection/emitted events use `response.model_id`, while role failure history and the `failures` result map use the outer key. That splits one physical response across two logical identities. PROPOSED_FIX: enforce `model_id == response.model_id` at ingestion and fail fast on mismatch.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.82  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` has no check that each active model was expected to respond exactly once, so duplicate and missing responses can coexist without detection.** Even ignoring the previously noted “missing responses treated as success-by-omission” issue, this code also accepts multiple logical responses from the same model if the caller uses inconsistent dict keys / payload IDs, and it never verifies cardinality against `active_models` or the allocation. That means the round-completion assumption feeding the FSM is ungrounded: `round_complete=True` is asserted without any completeness or uniqueness proof. PROPOSED_FIX: validate the response set against the expected active/allotted model set with exact-once semantics before failure detection and FSM advancement.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`update_fingerprints()` can crash on a response-only active model if `_live_fingerprints` lacks that ID, because active membership is not guaranteed to be a subset of the original pool.** The method iterates `for model_id in self.failure_handler.active_models:` and immediately does `old_fp = self._live_fingerprints[model_id]`. If earlier bad input introduced a foreign model into failure-handler state or active-set management drifts, this becomes a `KeyError`. This is a cross-area invariant break: Area 6 can admit arbitrary IDs while the adaptive loop assumes a closed world. PROPOSED_FIX: enforce closed-world model identity globally and guard `update_fingerprints()` with explicit membership validation before dereferencing `_live_fingerprints`.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.73  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The system can report `converged=True` and `stop=True` simultaneously on the same round, but the API provides no resolution or precedence at the result layer.** The FSM priority chooses `CONVERGED` over `DIMINISHED`, yet `RoundResult` stores both booleans independently. A caller inspecting only `RoundResult.converged`/`stop` cannot tell which reason actually drove termination without separately inspecting FSM state/reason. This is a cross-cutting semantic inconsistency between Area 3 and the orchestration API. PROPOSED_FIX: store the selected termination decision/event explicitly in `RoundResult` and/or expose a single authoritative stop reason field.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.71  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Input dataclasses and runtime computations accept negative finite values for core physical quantities, producing nonsensical but silently processed states.** Beyond NaN/inf concerns already raised elsewhere, there is no validation preventing negative `response_time`, negative `token_demand`, negative `L_std`, negative `cost`, negative `severity`, negative `criticality`, or negative `round_cost`. Several paths then treat these as meaningful: negative cost can invert marginal-value economics, negative token demand reduces model load, and negative response time avoids timeout checks. PROPOSED_FIX: add non-negativity/range validation to core dataclasses and manager entry points for all physical/count/probability fields.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.76  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`process_round()` emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` before any processing, before failures are handled, and before the FSM transition may fail, so event consumers can observe completion for a round that never successfully completed.** Prior findings noted confusing event semantics generally, but this is a sharper orchestration flaw: the method announces completion at entry, then may later discover a critical failure or even raise before appending results. Downstream monitors treating `ROUND_COMPLETE` as a commit point will be wrong. PROPOSED_FIX: emit a distinct `ROUND_PROCESSING_START` event at entry and reserve `ROUND_COMPLETE` for successful post-commit completion.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.68  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector.add_round_findings()` and `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round()` allow silent overwrites of prior round data, and `DynamicManager.process_round()` does not defend against replay of an existing round index.** This is broader than the specific BLIND/SYNTH index collision already found: even with unique indices, a caller can process the same round twice or mutate historical metrics by reinvoking the add methods for an existing `round_idx`. The caches are invalidated/recomputed, so prior history is not append-only. PROPOSED_FIX: make round ingestion append-only by rejecting duplicate `round_idx` unless an explicit overwrite mode is requested for recovery/testing.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.64  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`RoleAssignment.reassign(round_idx, ...)` accepts `round_idx` but never uses it, which masks a deeper design hole: failure-history penalties are unbounded lifetime averages with no temporal locality.** This is more than an unused parameter nuisance. Because `phi_hist = mean(all recorded failures)` over the entire run, ancient failures permanently depress COL suitability even after sustained recovery, and the provided `round_idx` offers no recency windowing or round-scoped computation. PROPOSED_FIX: either remove `round_idx` and document lifetime averaging, or use it to compute a bounded/windowed/decayed penalty consistent with adaptive reassignment.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.70  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The event callback path is not failure-isolated, so an observer exception can abort manager logic mid-operation and leave internal state half-updated.** `ManagerEventStream.emit()` directly calls the callback, and `FailureHandler._emit_event()` calls into that path during detection. A callback exception during failure detection or metric emission aborts `process_round()` immediately. This is stronger than merely “not exception-safe buffering”: it lets external observability code become a control-plane kill switch for the manager. PROPOSED_FIX: isolate observer failures—catch callback exceptions, record them as monitoring faults, and preserve core manager state progression.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.67  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`CorrelatedFailureModel.set_vulnerability()` permits self-vulnerability entries that are later unreachable and semantically inconsistent with `get_vulnerability()`.** Calling `set_vulnerability("m1", "m1", 0.2)` stores `frozenset({"m1"}) -> 0.2`, but `get_vulnerability("m1", "m1")` always returns `1.0` before consulting the map. That creates dead, contradictory state and indicates the API accepts an invalid pair shape. PROPOSED_FIX: reject `model_i == model_j` in `set_vulnerability()` and reserve self-correlation as an implicit identity case only.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.59  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.62  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`validate_all_reductions()` is not robust to validator assertions and can terminate the whole self-test suite prematurely instead of reporting structured failures.** Several validators use `assert` internally rather than returning booleans only. If one assertion fails, `validate_all_reductions()` raises and aborts the report, so the module may not produce a full pass/fail matrix. PROPOSED_FIX: make validators pure boolean checks or wrap each validator call in exception handling that records failure details without aborting the test harness.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.60  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The manager never emits `MODEL_RESPONSE` events despite advertising that event type in the public monitoring API.** This is a missing integration point spanning the monitoring interface and orchestration logic: response ingestion occurs in `process_round()`, yet no per-response progress event is produced. Consumers relying on the declared event taxonomy cannot observe response arrival/processing granularity. PROPOSED_FIX: emit `MODEL_RESPONSE` once per accepted response, after identity validation and before failure classification.

FINDING_ID: ROUND4_F015  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION: 0.58  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The top-level design claim “All six areas … are implemented as callable classes and functions matching the interface contracts from the converged plan” is overstated because multiple public methods expose internal mutable semantics rather than contract-stable snapshots.** `role_map` is shared by reference across subsystems, `process_round()` stores caller-owned inputs by reference, and several APIs return mutable numpy-backed structures. This is not a new single bug so much as a cross-cutting contract mismatch: the implementation behaves like a permissive in-process object graph, not a robust management layer with defensive boundaries. PROPOSED_FIX: define and enforce ownership/snapshot semantics at public API boundaries—copy inputs on ingestion, return immutable views/snapshots, and stop sharing internal dicts by reference.

Definitive stance: there are still missed findings; the most important new ones are the lack of a post-terminal guard in `process_round()`, unchecked foreign/mismatched response identities, and the resulting cross-area invariant breaks.
